name: Should I choose a low-threshold shower or a true roll-in shower?

mainEntity.name: Should I choose a low-threshold shower or a true roll-in shower?

acceptedAnswer.text: A low-threshold shower is not automatically the same as a roll-in shower. A low-threshold design reduces the step, while a roll-in design is planned for wheeled entry and may require more floor, drain, slope, and waterproofing work. Context: Published guidance notes that curbless construction can require a custom pan and substantial floor work. Elite Remodeling & Design can compare these approaches within the existing bathroom and intended use. Key factors: wheelchair dimensions, transfer method, available room length, drain location, floor height, caregiver space, and water containment. Practical guidance: Ask for two layouts with the entry, seat, controls, and drainage clearly shown. Compare accessibility, construction complexity, maintenance, and cost rather than focusing only on the threshold.
acceptedAnswer.description: Choose a low-threshold shower when a small step is manageable and room conditions limit reconstruction. Choose a roll-in shower when wheeled entry is needed and the floor, drain, slope, waterproofing, and surrounding clearances can support it. Compare both layouts before selecting materials.
